title: Android: Supported devices reduced if changing from gl_compatibility to mobile renderer
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in 4.5.stable, 4.5.1.stable ### System information N/A ### Issue description Exporting an Android project with the rendering method set to `mobile` leads to a significant drop in supported devices on Play Store. This is unexpected, since `mobile` according to documentation\* should fallback to `gl_compatibility` if not supported. Thus I would expect the number of supported devices to be equal or greater; not fewer. The only changes between the 2 versions in the above screenshot are: * `version_code` incremented by 1 (required to be unique per upload, does not affect supported devices) * `rendering/renderer/rendering_method.mobile` changed from `gl_compatibility` to `mobile`. Everything else is identical. The project has Gradle Build enabled, exporting to AAB, `armeabi-v7a` + `arm64-v8a`. \* Documentation: > Since Godot 4.4, when using Forward+ or Mobile, if Vulkan is not supported, the engine will fall back to Direct3D 12 and vice versa. If the attempted fallback driver is not supported either, the engine will then fall back to Compatibility when the RenderingDevice backend is not supported. This allows the project to run anyway, but it may look different than the intended appearance due to the more limited renderer. This behavior can be disabled in the project settings by unchecking [Rendering > Rendering Device > Fallback to OpenGL 3] \- https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/rendering/renderers.html If this **is** expected behavior, it would be beneficial to have a note in the documentation regarding this. ### Steps to reproduce Export and upload any project to Google Play Store, with rendering method set to `mobile` vs `gl_compatibility`. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
